To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined the contact angle and the curvature of the three-phase contact line of water on a silver nanoparticle on a scale of 1 nm and that we have shown that the microscopic contact angle is smaller than the macroscopic one due to negative line tension.
we were able to determine the contact angle and the line tension for a liquid droplet nucleating on a solid surface on a scale of 1 nm.
we were able to directly determine the microscopic contact angle for water on silver nanoparticles, and that this contact angle is significantly smaller than the macroscopic contact angle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental properties of wetting on the nanoscale.
the wetting of nano-objects.
the wetting of solid surfaces by water in the presence of a third immiscible phase (air).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the contact angles on the molecular scale are smaller than the macroscopically determined contact angles.

the wetting of nano objects can be understood by the same principles as the wetting of macroscopic objects, but the contact angle is no more a constant but rather a variable depending on the size of the object.
the microscopic contact angle is the result of a balance between the surface energy and the line tension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can determine the contact angle on a nearly molecular scale.
we can now measure and understand the wetting of nanoparticles on the molecular scale.
we have been able to directly determine contact line properties on the molecular scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contact angle is not a macroscopically defined quantity.
the wetting of nano-objects is fundamentally different from the wetting of macroscopic objects.
the contact line curvature can be used as a tool to measure contact angles on the molecular scale.
